chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Khashab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from the one who reported concerning the dung-eaters.
He said: There is no problem with eating them when they are mixed (with normal feed).

key_terms.الْجَلَّالَاتِ: Jallalat: animals whose meat is affected by eating impure substances (dung, filth); a specific fiqh category
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: La ba's: there is no objection/problem; a standard jurisprudential phrase granting permissibility
key_terms.يُخْلَطْنَ: They are mixed; refers to mixing normal clean feed with the animals' diet to purify them

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the meat of dung-eating animals (jallalat) in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the jurisprudential question of whether the meat of jallalat — animals that habitually consume filth or dung — is permissible to eat. The Imam rules that if these animals are fed normal feed mixed with their usual diet, their meat becomes permissible. This reflects the broader Islamic legal principle that an impure state can be remediated through a process of purification or dietary change (known as istibraa), making the animal lawful for consumption.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Khashab, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from the one who reported it,
‘With regards to the dung-eaters. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it when it is mixed (with other feed)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Khashshab from Ali ibn Asbat from the one who narrated to him

who has narrated the following: “About animals that feed on feces he (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If the feed of an animal is mixed with other feed besides feces, then it is not unlawful to use it for food.’”
